question: Which TodoMVC hash-SPA variants exhibit URL-level leakage below 40% and sufficient title variation, enabling >=50 non-leakage transitions for PMI analysis — thereby identifying suitable production-like testbeds to bridge the synthetic-to-real gap in the C-WEB-DYNAMICS research program?
hypothesis: TodoMVC hash-SPA variants with client-side routing (where multiple views share the same URL path, e.g., #/active, #/completed) exhibit lower URL-level leakage than server-rendered MPAs (78-92%), because hash-based navigation allows multiple states per URL and client-side transitions (button clicks, form submissions, JavaScript-triggered) produce non-link-leakage transitions. At least 1 of 5 variants achieves <40% leakage, enabling >=50 NL transitions at manageable raw collection sizes (~83 raw at 40% leakage).
falsifier: The claim is falsified if ANY of: (1) ALL 5 TodoMVC variants exhibit leakage >=40%; OR (2) ALL variants have <2 unique document.title values; OR (3) ALL variants have achievable NL count <50 at 500 raw collection limit (achievable_NL = 500 * (1 - leakage_rate)); OR (4) positive control (Wikipedia) leakage <80% (confirming measurement validity); OR (5) data quality insufficient (<100 raw transitions per variant).
baselines: Server-rendered MPA baseline: Wikipedia leakage rate 91.2% from parent (EXP-PHYSICS-35185288822). Expected high leakage (>80%). Provides within-experiment comparison: the ONLY difference is site type (MPA vs SPA).

Frequency baseline: P(transition_type) marginal distribution of link clicks vs button clicks vs form submissions vs JavaScript-triggered across all variants. Expected link-dominated on MPAs, mixed on SPAs.

Achievable NL baseline: 50 NL transitions at 40% leakage requires 83 raw transitions; at 80% leakage requires 250 raw transitions; at 92% leakage requires 625 raw transitions. Provides feasibility threshold for PMI analysis.
positive_control: TodoMVC vanilla JS hash-SPA (known structure: multiple views share URL #/active, #/completed, #/). Expected leakage <60% and >=2 unique titles. Pass criterion: leakage <60% AND unique_titles >=2 AND raw_transitions >=100. This validates the measurement pipeline on a known SPA structure before testing other variants.
null_control: Wikipedia (known high leakage server-rendered MPA). Expected leakage >80%. Pass criterion: leakage >80% AND unique_titles >=2 AND raw_transitions >=100. This confirms the measurement pipeline correctly identifies high leakage on known MPAs.
measurement_validity: 5 TodoMVC variants: vanilla JS (ES6), React, Vue, Angular, Svelte. All use hash-based client-side routing. URLs: todomvc.com/examples/{vanillajs,react,vue,angular,svelte}/

Browser-based collection: Playwright headless Chrome, collect per-transition: URL (before and after), document.title (before and after), action target (href or element), action primitive (click, submit, type, keypress), timestamp.
Minimum 100 raw transitions per variant (20+ unique URLs, 3+ action types).

Title variation check: each variant must have >= 2 unique document.title values across collected transitions. Variants with constant title are flagged but not excluded (may indicate title=URL coupling).
Leakage definition: action.target_href == state_after.url (same as parent). URL normalization: strip trailing slash, decode percent-encoding, ignore fragment changes within same path.
Achievable NL count: 500 * (1 - leakage_rate). Threshold: >=50 NL at 500 raw.
Action type stratification: record action_primitive for each transition (link_click, button_click, form_submit, keypress, javascript). Compute per-type leakage rates.
Session diversity: at least 5 distinct browsing sessions per variant (different starting points, action sequences).
No authentication required (TodoMVC is publicly accessible).
Playwright EPIPE mitigation: use single-page context per session, close browser between sessions, do not close context before page load complete.
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) >=1/5 variants achieve leakage <40% AND achievable_NL >=50 at 500 raw AND (2) >=1/5 variants have >=2 unique titles AND (3) positive control (Wikipedia) leakage >80% AND (4) null control (TodoMVC vanilla JS) leakage <60% AND (5) >=100 raw transitions per variant AND (6) >=5 sessions per variant — verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST (SPA approach viable for PMI analysis). If 0/5 variants achieve leakage <40% AND achievable_NL >=50 — verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (SPA approach not viable for URL-level PMI on these variants). If controls fail or data quality insufficient — verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: TodoMVC hash-SPA variants with <40% leakage are suitable testbeds for title-aware PMI experiments. SPIDER should target these SPAs for the next C-WEB-DYNAMICS experiment, directly addressing the synthetic-to-real gap. The pivot to SPAs is justified. Specific variants with lowest leakage become priority targets.
product_consequence_negative: All TodoMVC variants exhibit >=40% leakage, making URL-level PMI analysis infeasible at manageable collection sizes. SPIDER should reconsider state representation (e.g., DOM, accessibility tree, visual layout) or abandon URL-level PMI approach for SPAs. The pivot to SPAs is not justified. The dominant synthetic-to-real gap persists.
estimated_cost: Low: 5 TodoMVC variants (publicly accessible, no auth), browser-based collection (~2-3 hours total including setup, data collection, and analysis), Python analysis (~1 hour). No model calls required. Estimated 3-4 hours total.
expected_information_gain: Very high: directly addresses the dominant bottleneck across the entire C-WEB-DYNAMICS research program — the synthetic-to-real gap (30+ experiments, all synthetic or locally-hosted). A positive result (>=1 variant with <40% leakage) provides concrete targets for the next PMI experiment and justifies the SPA pivot. A negative result (all variants >=40% leakage) kills the SPA pivot approach and forces reconsideration of state representation. Either outcome resolves the dominant unknown and enables a targeted go/no-go decision on title-based state representation for production SPAs.
